tagline: Andaman's mainland gateway — limestone-island demand, boat-only nodes.
summary: Krabi is the Andaman mainland hub feeding a dense archipelago (Phi Phi, Hong, Poda, Railay) and the Ao Nang tourist node. Much of its signature geography — Railay peninsula, the island parks — is road-inaccessible and water-only, making it a structural fit for a quiet, zero-wake electric shuttle. Krabi pairs with Phuket across the ~18nm Andaman corridor.

demand_signals.detail: Ao Nang/Nopparat Thara is one of Thailand's densest day-trip launch points to Hong, Poda, Chicken Island, Phi Phi.
Railay peninsula has no road link — every arrival is by boat, a captive shuttle market.

use_cases: Ao Nang <-> Railay premium beach shuttle

journeys.note: Andaman cross-corridor; needs range-gate confirm in monsoon swell.

navier_fit: High. Mix of very short captive hops (Ao Nang-Railay) and mid-range island/cross corridors within Pioneer II range; road-inaccessible nodes remove road-modal competition; multi-operator piers (Klong Jilad, Ao Nang) ease pedestal siting.
competitive_landscape: Dense longtail + speedboat operators (Ao Nang Longtail Boat Club controls Railay access); all diesel/2-stroke, noise- and wake-heavy — a quiet electric shuttle is a clean differentiator.
seasonality: Peak: Nov-Apr dry season. SW monsoon May-Oct raises Andaman swell; range-gate cross-corridors, keep short captive hops year-round.
regulatory_note: Thai cabotage; Marine Department domestic licensing. Railay longtail cartel is a real access-politics factor — partner-of-record / local-operator structure advised.

precedents.label: Ao Nang-Railay longtail shuttle
precedents.note: Established captive water-only route, diesel today

grab.super_app_fit: Grab in-app island-transfer + Ao Nang-Railay shuttle booking with GrabCar pier handoff at Klong Jilad / Ao Nang.
grab.wedge: Own the road-inaccessible Railay shuttle as a pre-booked premium lane inside Grab — no road-modal alternative exists.
